sanity_expectations: m is positive and real over the entire sampled region
at fixed H and P, m increases monotonically as T decreases below Tc (order parameter rises as reduced temperature 1-T/Tc grows)
m -> 0 as T -> Tc (t_red -> 0), rising steeply just below the transition
m approaches a finite saturation of order m0 (~1) as T -> low end (t_red -> ~0.9)
increasing H slightly reduces m via the demagnetizing factor, most noticeably at high field and deep in the ordered phase

Strongest at T~12.8 (t_red~0.87, deep in ordered phase), H~9.96 (high field), P~1.81 — i.e. where the field-response variable x is largest. All terms visible; no weak terms.
role_corrections: T: input/axis -> independent variable (confirmed; temperature sampling axis, gets range)
H: input/axis -> independent variable (confirmed; applied-field axis, gets range)
P: input/axis -> independent variable (confirmed; pressure axis, gets range)
Tc: input/axis -> PARAMETER (overridden: critical temperature is a fixed physical constant setting the scale of T, not a sampled axis)
m0, beta, a_corr, Delta, w_fluc, t_cross, chi_H, delta_H, P_ref, gamma_p, gamma_p2, kappa_p, b_demag: parameters (confirmed, fixed to physical constants)
rationale: Structural analysis shows an explicit, algebraically solvable relation for m with no derivatives or integrals -> equation_type=explicit, integrator=evaluate_explicit. Dependent variable is m (LHS). The three genuine sampling axes are T (temperature), H (applied field), and P (pressure); Tc was mislabeled as an axis but is a fixed critical-temperature constant, so it is demoted to a parameter. Ranges chosen to keep the reduced temperature t_red=1-T/Tc in (0.01, 0.9): T in [10,99] with Tc=100 captures both the steep rise near Tc and saturation far below. H in [0,10] spans zero-field baseline up to fields where the field-response variable x=O(1) and the new demag term becomes visible. P in [-2,2] around P_ref=0 exercises the pressure terms. Physical parameter values: beta=0.35 (3D critical exponent), Delta=0.5 (Wegner), delta_H=4.8 (critical-isotherm exponent), b_demag=0.3 (within suggested 0-0.5). check_substitution confirms finite/real output; excitation_check confirms all terms including the new demag factor are well above 5*sigma.

scenario_text: A magnetic material near its ordering transition is studied by measuring its spontaneous order parameter as the temperature is tuned below a critical point. Just below the transition the order parameter rises steeply from zero, while far below it saturates. The measurement captures how the ordered fraction depends on how far the system sits beneath the critical temperature.
